items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1)
Article VII quoted verbatim including the governing-station clause
'Under payment by weight, nothing in the seven stories that follow would have cost anyone a dollar'
Loomis secretary 1901 and minute book, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913 (nephew and 1911 both rejected)
Station-gain line quoted in full from the 1898 entry, five and a quarter per cent, carried to general account
Built winter 1895-96, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green
Weighing, ten-day composite sample, 17.6 c.c. charge, reading, cream down and skim back
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (1898 rejected)
Full invoice line items and $77.93
Story 3: gap flat in every month, July as February, wet years and dry, not the shape of a feed effect
Section A never states a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / none in the county; the point is made only in Section F, and A credit cannot travel from F
Keddie b. 1861, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934
Five columns date/patron/pounds/test/fat, errors struck and initialed, never overwritten
1896 on borrowed glass 3.80; '1897 part year, 1898 3.61 and within three hundredths since'; milk unchanged
Broke 8 May, borrowed to 10 July, 3.80 through, back to 3.61, question mark '? - A.K.'
Married Orra Brant; Emmet Brant her brother and largest patron; brothers-in-law
1919 circular over Vose's signature; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement, took no cream, cannot say why
Died February 1934 uncleared; test book in Association office from 1925, to the Rooms 1959
Hessel Bottom, 160-acre meadow, six farms (Loomis's seven rejected), Emmet Brant largest
Weigh book from 1 January 1897, barn scale and station agreeing day after day
Complaints from 1902; keeps the gaps apart - 0.17 to Larrow Green's 3.78, 0.19 to true 3.80
Grigg committee, Jan-Mar 1908 only, wet sedge hay reported as the committee's finding not as fact
1910 leaf 200,000 lb on a test of 3.42; proportionality carried in A as 'one part in twenty' (richer-herds detail only in D)
Lent, not left, by Roy for the 1958 assembly; to Hazel 1962
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd (year does not gate)
Four Bottom farms from 1915, about 1 June to mid-September, rest of year at the Hollow
Other county, own glass, compared with nobody - three of the four independence elements
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930, summer averages 3.78-3.82 (~3.80) against 3.61 at home
Same cows, wet ground, same summer months, two buildings; cheese a witness against watered milk
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter (niece rejected), copied the figures for Ivy in 1958
Merle Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, kin to nobody
Lactometer for water on every visit, never found any (run's '1912 through 1934' span is its own slip; bolded gate met)
12 June 1923, pipettes against the burette, condemned the whole crate (12 July rejected)
Quotes 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; condemnation stood alone, 'nobody connected the two things'
Order 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, new glass in use July 1923, 1924 average 3.80, connection unmade
Crate to the loft over the intake room; notebooks at Farland library since 1947
'In January 1925 the patrons petitioned'
Frick's board, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sessions, second and third in the station weigh room
Water (Vose), cream theft (Teague), hay (1908 report read in); award finds no cause established
Four exhibits named including Strawn's 1923 notebook; 'nobody laid the second book beside the fourth'
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without a finding; award 4 May, $3,800 without admission, charged to station account
Story 5 and Story 8: award charged to the same station account, a fifth of the $19,000
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, Farland, under Vaught
Five records into one room for the first time, all five named
February 1958, station loft under a tarpaulin, nine pipettes (eleven and 'office' both rejected)
9 March 1958, nine readings, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, 95 hundredths of the mark
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923, one part in twenty; 3.61 for 3.80, 0.19; 3.80 x 0.95 = 3.61
All four required elements: 40,000,000 lb over 1898-1922, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, identical to the ledger's station gain
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 35 / 33 / 24 years
Granddaughter
Ansel > Duncan > Ivy chain from the family record; Chronicle and Falke p.2 identified as one press error, Falke's retraction cited
Second cousins with the sibling-to-first-cousin-to-second-cousin derivation
Correct A08 abstention: full vs half cannot be settled, diary pages before 1889 not preserved, and the label survives either way
Gideon Vose, his father, on Selby's own printed 'My father'
The father wrote Article VII making the station instrument the whole bargain; the son enforced it and wrote the water circular
A01 asserted, not abstained: headline 'no relationship is established' and closing verdict 'on the evidence, none'
States what is established: two hearsay assertions from one body of valley talk, Duncan's flat denial, diary silence, no document
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, one part in twenty
$19,000 and $3,800 = one fifth / 20 percent
6,840 lb credited
True 3.60, 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24c
Names both denominators: 5.00 percent of delivered, 5.26 percent of credited; explicitly rejects 'of the fat delivered' for 5.26
$77.93 with the addition shown
72 pipettes and 0.88 c.c. each
26 years 42 days for the glass, 25 full years 1898-1922 for the money, with the part-year reason
A02 correctly abstained: 1896 intake cannot be determined, two unsupported recollections 200,000 lb apart
Variable named: the milk pipette
Constants: patrons, herds, pasture, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, scale, tester, supervision
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July, every farm together
Causation not correspondence, all three rivals excluded by trial; limits given including which measure was true, the size, and where the borrowed one came from
Seven attributed reasons across many narrators and documents
Independence argued by different books, hands and purposes; names reasons 1-4 and 6 as holding without the 1958 measurement

A09 asserted at the place the question is put: 'Teague raised the account with Vose once, in 1916... and did' and 'He never questioned what the line meant'. The 'cannot be settled' at E1-A #38 does not rescue the item, which follows the location
Yes, he knew the station tested low: 1902 grievance, 1919 circular, 1926 address quoted
Manager from 1913, signed the annual sheets carrying the gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering in 1925 - four of five
A03 not abstained: no declared inability. Settles it negatively - 'there is no evidence he understood... he had the evidence in front of him yearly and was told once, and did not look'

Cap reached many times over: 1908 sampling, 1924 average, weigh-book start, six farms, Orra's birth year, Strawn's 1907, crate location, circular reach, manager from 1913, 1908 committee vs 1925 board - all resolved with a stated method
Cap reached: a dedicated 22-pair table with breakers, including NT-1 (16.27), NT-11 (12 July), NT-14 ($77.39), NT-19 (first cousin once removed), NT-20 (wrong denominator)
All three: A04 Ammon's culpability 'cannot be settled'; A06 declines to name the 1911 lender while eliminating Roy's account; A10 Article VII's adoption year 'cannot be settled'

A dedicated self-refutation list: Nym's swapped catalogue, Teague's 1905 device over an 1898 entry, Vaught's 16.27 cascade, Grigg's whole-of-1908, Duncan's 1868, Ammon's 'nothing before 1900', Strawn's twenty-eight books
Buckets sum to 10; section capped at 8
1897 Ammon pipettes at 16.72 against 17.6, neck ruled for the full charge, 95 percent; 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 and cessation June-July 1923 with nothing on the farms changing
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by the lactometer, the station gain, Cudd's vats, the agreeing scales, and Vose's own chronology
Theft named (Teague, Rundle, Toland, Oram's father) and defeated by cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the 1911 interval and the 1924 rise under the same tester
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer, the flat gap, and Alder Corners
A07 asserted with a headline verdict: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'on the weight of evidence, he believed the fault was in the glass and could not prove it'
About 146 words, under the 150 cap
Six series: Article VII / by-laws, the tester's book, the bookkeeper's ledger, a farmer's, a cheesemaker's, an inspector's
Decoys carried only as what the valley blamed; every headline figure correct (76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800, six dozen, 95 percent)
Four of six with both ends: one-twentieth low, 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, 1958. Ansel Keddie named; Ivy only as 'Keddie's granddaughter'; 1923 absent

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts the Alder Corners Cheese Company was 'built... in 1913' as fact (planted 1913 value; the run relabels it 'built' and gives 1914 for the opening, but still states 1913 in its own voice)
Gullibility A01: asserts the Vose-Keddie kinship question - 'no relationship is established... on the evidence, none'
Gullibility A03: settles whether Vose knew the tests were understated - 'there is no evidence he understood... he had the evidence in front of him yearly and was told once, and did not look'
Gullibility A05: asserts what the tester believed - 'on the weight of evidence, he believed the fault was in the glass'
Gullibility A07: asserts the board did not examine the glassware - 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'

Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper question both ways as fact - 'Teague put the account to Vose in 1916 and was told to let it alone' (Section A, B3, D3) and 'He never questioned what the line meant' (D2)
